samples.summary: No test covers the PKCE challenge flowing from the consumed state into the minted code — the whole protection could be silently disabled and the suite stays green
samples.evidence: auth.controller.ts:126 is the only place `state.codeChallenge` is carried onto the authorization code (`createCode(user.id, state.codeChallenge)`). Every test of that path in auth.controller.spec.ts creates state without a challenge: line 193 `createState('cli', 9876)` and line 221 `createState('cli', 9876, 'n0nce-x/y')` (third arg is the nonce, not the challenge), and neither test then redeems the resulting code. The `PKCE binding` describe (spec lines 347–410) bypasses the callback entirely by calling `cliAuthStore.createCode(42, challenge)` directly. So if the controller were changed to `createCode(user.id)` — dropping the challenge and turning every CLI code back into a bearer — no test in the repo fails. Likewise github-auth.guard.spec.ts only asserts the challenge reaches the store, never that it reaches a code. The end-to-end binding (guard → state → code → exchange) is untested.
searchedFor: grep for createState/createCode usages in backend auth specs
read cli-auth.store.ts to confirm arg order

samples.summary: No test that the redirect omits `state` when the login carried no nonce; the existing regex assertion passes either way
samples.evidence: The new `stateEcho` branch (auth.controller.ts:130-132) has two arms. The nonce arm is covered (spec line 218). The empty arm is only exercised by the pre-existing test at spec line 190, whose assertion is `expect.stringMatching(/^http:\/\/127\.0\.0\.1:9876\/callback\?code=.+/)` — that matches a URL with `&state=...` appended just as happily, so it cannot detect a stray or wrong echo when no nonce was minted.

samples.summary: Optional-chaining assertions in the guard spec also hold when no state was stored at all, so they don't distinguish 'value dropped' from 'CLI login not registered'
samples.evidence: `stateFor()` returns `undefined` when the guard set no `__cliStateToken` (spec lines 44-49). Assertions such as `expect(stateFor({...nonce: overBound})?.nonce).toBeUndefined()` (line 67-69) and the empty/array-nonce cases (lines 72-80) are satisfied by `undefined?.nonce` — i.e. they pass even if the guard stopped creating state for CLI logins entirely. Only the separate 'still issues a state token' test (line 82) constrains that, and it uses a different query shape. Asserting on the state object first (e.g. `expect(state).toBeDefined()`) would make these tests able to fail for the reason they claim.
searchedFor: read github-auth.guard.ts to confirm token is only set inside the port branch

samples.summary: The new `codeVerifier` DTO validation (@IsOptional/@IsString/@Length(43,128)) has no test; controller specs call the method directly and bypass the validation pipe
samples.evidence: auth.dto.ts adds `@Length(43, 128)` on `codeVerifier`, but every exercise of the field goes through `controller.cliExchange({...})` in auth.controller.spec.ts (lines 361-409), which never runs class-validator. The bounds are therefore unasserted — and spec line 403 passes `codeVerifier: 'nope'` (4 chars), a value the shipped validation pipe would reject before the controller is reached, so that test exercises a state unreachable in production.

verdict.reason: The finding is real. auth.controller.ts:126 (`createCode(user.id, state.codeChallenge)`) is the sole carry-over of the PKCE challenge from state to authorization code, and nothing tests it. The two CLI-callback tests (auth.controller.spec.ts:193, :221) build state with no challenge — the third positional arg of `createState(mode, port, nonce?, codeChallenge?)` (cli-auth.store.ts:42-47) is the nonce — and neither redeems the resulting code, asserting only on the redirect URL. The `PKCE binding` block (auth.controller.spec.ts:347-410) mints codes directly with `cliAuthStore.createCode(42, challenge)`, skipping the callback. github-auth.guard.spec.ts:88-96 stops at the state. cli-auth.store.spec.ts never mentions codeChallenge. The CLI-side test (packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts:111-132) stubs global fetch for /auth/cli/exchange, so the controller never executes. A repo-wide grep for `CliAuthStore|cliAuthStore` returns only 7 files (store, guard, module, controller and their 3 specs), which bounds where such a test could exist, and the backend e2e specs contain no /auth/github/callback or /auth/cli/exchange flow. Replacing line 126 with `createCode(user.id)` — silently disabling PKCE for every CLI login — would leave the whole suite green. This is a security-relevant behavior with no meaningful test, squarely a major test-adequacy gap.

finding.summary: New `failFromBackend` login error envelope has no test on any of its three call sites
finding.evidence: `login.ts` replaces three prose `console.error(...)+process.exit(1)` failure paths (token exchange, `/auth/me`, `/workspaces`) with `failFromBackend`, which parses the backend body and emits `backendErrorEnvelope(...)`. The only login test (`packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts`) mocks every backend call to return `jsonResponse(...)` with status 200, so no test ever drives a non-ok response through `failFromBackend`. Grepping `packages/cli/test` for `failFromBackend`, `Token exchange failed`, `Failed to fetch user info` returns nothing. Untested consequences include whether the envelope is actually emitted once, whether the message survives, and whether execution really stops (the call sites `await` a helper typed `Promise<never>` while the code after continues to `exchangeRes.json()`).

verdict.reason: The finding claims no test drives a non-ok response through `failFromBackend` and that the only login test mocks all backend calls to 200. That is false. `packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts:170-246` is a second test, `it('reports a rejected exchange as the one-line error envelope')`, that mocks `/auth/cli/exchange` to return HTTP 401 with a Nest-shaped body (lines 194-206), runs the real `registerLoginCommand` action end-to-end (lines 175, 214) with the real `backendErrorEnvelope` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:118) unmocked, and asserts exactly the three consequences the finding calls untested: the envelope is emitted once and on one line (`toHaveLength(1)`, `not.toContain('\n')`, lines 236-238); the backend's own message survives rather than the login.ts:85 fallback (`JSON.parse(...)` equals `{error:{code:'UNAUTHORIZED',message:'Invalid or expired code',command:'login'}}`, lines 239-245); and execution actually stops rather than falling through to `exchangeRes.json()` (process.exit stubbed to throw at 182-186, asserting rejection `exit:1`, `exit` called with 1, and `expect(exchanges).toBe(1)` at line 234). The test comment at line 167 names `failFromBackend` directly. The other two call sites (login.ts:100, login.ts:119) use the identical helper, so at most this is a minor breadth gap, not the claimed absence of any coverage.
